previous_assumption: RentalCompanyAuctionPanel assumed a Rental Company could always fetch full AuctionDetail (via getAuctionDetail) for any live auction it discovered through getActiveAuctionForRequirement, using that detail response alone to decide whether to show the "Request to join" button.
correction: AuctionService.getAuctionDetail deliberately 404s for a caller that isn't the auction's owner and isn't yet a participant (participant isolation, tested in auction-service.test.ts: "hides an auction entirely from an organization that never joined it") — this is intentional, locked behavior, not a bug, and was NOT changed. The real bug was the frontend calling getAuctionDetail before the Rental Company had ever joined, so a live auction it was eligible to bid on would either show a scary "Auction not found" error or (after the first fix in this session) silently render as "No auction running" — a Rental Company could never discover or join a real live auction. Fixed entirely on the frontend: `auction` state now comes from `getActiveAuctionForRequirement` alone (which already carries biddingDirection/basePrice/status/dates and is NOT participant-gated); `getAuctionDetail` is still called, but its 404 is now caught and treated as "not yet a participant" rather than propagated — the pre-join UI (header + "Request to join" button) renders entirely from the `auction` summary, and the participant/bids/result view only renders once `detail` is actually populated (i.e. after joining). Lesson: when a "detail" endpoint is intentionally gated behind participation/ownership for a real security reason, don't weaken it — restructure the caller to use a broader, ungated "summary" endpoint for the pre-authorization UI state instead.
